messages.author: bccf789db78f8994
messages.subject: SNP Associations for F2
parts:
Hi there,

I have another question about the qtl2 package. I want to pull out the SNP associations and eventually the corresponding gene plot. I have a cvs with the MUGA genotypes for each strain in my F2 cross. I modified this cvs to look like the data file used in the user guide DO example but when I attempt to calculate the strain distribution pattern an error reports that there are no polymorphic markers. The only notable difference that I can think of between my file and the example file is that it contains all of the markers from the MUGA data set, rather than a region specific to a marker. 

Is there a better way to do this?

Thanks so much!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: SNP Associations for F2
parts:
The SNP association analysis that we do in the DO doesn't really apply for an F2 between two inbred strains, as there's no collapsing of multiple alleles that needs to occur. The results you get from scan1() are basically everything.

In plot_scan1, you could use type="p" or type="b" to have points plotted, if you want to see the LOD scores at individual markers.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] SNP Associations for F2
parts:
Similar to summary() in R/qtl1, find_peaks() has the default of just return in the largest LOD score on each chromosome. You can try to use the 'peakdrop' argument to get at secondary peaks on a chromosome, but I understand you're wanting to look at the results in more detail.

The output of scan1() is a matrix of LOD scores, with rows being positions and columns being phenotypes. You could try just viewing the rows the exceed a particular value.

This would print all of the rows where the maximum LOD score in that row is > 4:

max_by_row <- apply(my_scan1_output, 1, max)
my_scan1_output[ max_by_row > 4, ]

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] SNP Associations for F2
parts:
plot_pxg() takes some set of genotypes as input.
You could use table() on those genotypes to get a frequency table.

If you derived the inferred genotypes with maxmarg(), it could be that with the minprob argument you chose, there's only one genotype that was observed with at least that probability.

karl

> On Mar 11, 2018, at 6:38 PM, A Salvador <annacs...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Karl,
>
> Thanks for the taking the time to answer all of these questions.
>
> I was able to pull out the max LOD scores with your suggestion above and eventually find the markers of interest. Do you know of any reason why when I plot_pxg at these markers I would only see one genotype? It shouldn't appear in the max LOD scores if there were not two different genotypes present in the data, correct?
>
> I am using cM from the gmap to plot_pxg but, I have tried it with the Mbp position as well and no luck.
>
> Thanks!
> Anna
>
> On Tuesday, March 6, 2018 at 10:38:29 AM UTC-6, Karl Broman wrote:
> Similar to summary() in R/qtl1, find_peaks() has the default of just return in the largest LOD score on each chromosome. You can try to use the 'peakdrop' argument to get at secondary peaks on a chromosome, but I understand you're wanting to look at the results in more detail.
>
> The output of scan1() is a matrix of LOD scores, with rows being positions and columns being phenotypes. You could try just viewing the rows the exceed a particular value.
>
> This would print all of the rows where the maximum LOD score in that row is > 4:
>
> max_by_row <- apply(my_scan1_output, 1, max)
> my_scan1_output[ max_by_row > 4, ]
>
> karl
>
> > On Mar 5, 2018, at 3:43 PM, A Salvador <annacs...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > Right, maybe I am confused about that output then.
> >
> > I have 2 markers showing up just above the threshold for a phenotype. I am interested in understanding specifically which markers those are.
> >
> > I have used find_marker to locate the marker at the position reported in the output from find_peaks but, I'm not sure if this is necessarily the point at the highest part of the peak or, how to obtain the second point which is just below.
> >
> > Please, let me know if I haven't made any sense here!
> > Thanks so much!
> > Anna
> >
> > On Friday, March 2, 2018 at 5:39:38 PM UTC-6, Karl Broman wrote:
> > There’s a function find_peaks()
> >
> > karl

> >> How do we bring up the table with markers corresponding to the top LOD scores from our scan? I tried to adapt an old command, summary(out, threshold = 3.00), but it brings up quantiles for each phenotype.

> >> > The SNP association analysis that we do in the DO doesn't really apply for an F2 between two inbred strains, as there's no collapsing of multiple alleles that needs to occur. The results you get from scan1() are basically everything.
